title: Étale origin of constructible complexes locally of finite Tor dimension
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $A$ be a discrete commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Use the small étale and pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant coefficient sheaves $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $\nu_X^*$ for its inverse image on module sheaves, which is exact [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] and is applied termwise on derived categories.

For $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A_X)$, the following are equivalent:

1. Every $H^q(M)$ is constructible [def-sfb-affine-locally-constructible-proetale-modules], and $M$ locally has finite Tor dimension: for every site object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $a_i\leq b_i$ such that $H^q(M|_{U_i}\otimes^L_{A_X|_{U_i}}N_i)=0$ for every degree-zero module sheaf $N_i$ on the slice and every $q\notin[a_i,b_i]$. Slice restriction is [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and the K-flat derived tensor product over the constant ring sheaf and cohomology are [def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].
2. There are a bounded constructible complex $C\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ [def-pe-etale-constructible-module] and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C\simeq M$, with $C$ of finite Tor amplitude: there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(C\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ (étale K-flat derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]) for every degree-zero étale $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$.

No boundedness, completeness, or prior étale-origin assumption is imposed on $M$.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, parts (2) and (4) for n=1 and their proof (the uniform Tor interval on quasi-compact X, and étale origin via Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, with the 'small argument omitted' that the étale antecedent keeps the Tor interval); the converse direction from Tag 09AL and the Noetherian interval comparison.

proof.text: Assume (1). Since $X$ is quasi-compact, the local-to-global Tor lemma [lem-sfb-proetale-tor-local-global] applies to $M$ with the constant ring $A_X$: its condition (2) is word for word the local finite Tor dimension condition in (1), with the same slice restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction] and the same derived tensor [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Hence there are integers $a\leq b$ with $H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ for every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$. This is the uniform interval of the proof of Tag 09C2 ('By definition of locally having finite tor dimension, we can find $a,b$'); it covers also the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof, second sentence (uniform Tor interval on quasi-compact X)

proof.text: Take the degree-zero test module $N=A_X$. If $P\to M$ is a K-flat resolution, then $M\otimes^L_{A_X}A_X=P\otimes_{A_X}A_X\simeq P\simeq M$ by the definition of the derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Hence $H^q(M)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Together with the constructibility of every $H^q(M)$ assumed in (1), $M$ lies in the bounded constructible pro-étale category; boundedness has been deduced, not assumed.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, part (1) (boundedness $H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$), here from the unit test instead of derived completeness

proof.text: The bounded constructible comparison [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] applies: $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $A$ is discrete Noetherian, and the constructibility of its first paragraph (finite constructible locally closed stratifications locally on $X$, locally constant of finite type on each stratum) is the affine-local predicate of the item. Its equivalence $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)\to D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ given by $\nu_X^*$ is essentially surjective, so there are $C\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C\simeq M$. No completeness or torsion hypothesis on the coefficients is used.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof of part (4): 'follows from Lemma lemma-compare-constructible-derived' (Tag 09AL)

proof.text: Apply the fixed-interval Noetherian Tor comparison [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] to $C$ and the integers $a\leq b$ of step 1. Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ is invariant under isomorphism in the derived category, so $\nu_X^*C\simeq M$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$; the 'if' direction gives $H^q(C\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $A_X$-module sheaf $N$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$. This proves (2), and is the 'small argument omitted' of Tag 09C2 (4).

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof of part (4): 'L_n has finite tor dimension because K_n does (small argument omitted)'

proof.text:
Conversely assume (2), with $C$ and its interval $[a,b]$. Since $
u_X^*$ maps $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ into $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison], every $H^q(
u_X^*C)$, hence every $H^q(M)$, is constructible. The 'only if' direction of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] gives Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for $
u_X^*C$, hence for $M$. This is condition (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-tor-local-global], whose implication (1)⇒(2) gives, for every site object $U$, a covering of $U$ and intervals as required by the local finite Tor dimension condition in (1).

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived, and the converse of the uniformity sentence of the proof of Tag 09C2
